meta.homeTitle: Coded — The world is the classroom
meta.homeDescription: International STEAM programs for students aged 11–17 in Orlando, the UK and Tokyo.

hero.headline: The world is the classroom. Your project is the future.
hero.sub: International programs for students aged 11–17 in Orlando, the UK and Tokyo: expert-led workshops, real projects and a final project presentation.

method.title: Four steps, from classroom to project

experts.title: Expert delivered
experts.body: Classes are led by specialists who work in what they teach.

workshops.title: Live workshops
workshops.body: Students learn by doing, in the places where technology actually happens.

projects.title: Project-based learning
projects.body: Every team designs a solution to a real challenge and defends it at the end.

coding.title: Coding
coding.body: Code ties it all together: from idea to working prototype.

skills.title: What they bring back home
skills.sdg: Every project picks at least one of the UN Sustainable Development Goals.

championship.title: From your classroom to Tokyo.
championship.body: The top 20 winning schools from past leagues prepare for six months and present their project in Tokyo. The winning team gets a cash prize and Coded's support to make it real.

trust.title: They travel far. Never alone.

guardian.title: A Guardian for every student
guardian.body: Each student has a personal Guardian who shares updates and photos with the family every day.

doctor.title: On-site doctor
doctor.body: On-site medical care and arrangements with local healthcare providers.

insurance.title: Health insurance
insurance.body: Every student travels with health insurance included.

app.title: 360 navigation app
app.body: Families can follow the program's journey from the app.

staff.title: 24/7 staff at the residence
staff.body: Passcode or keypass access and on-site staff around the clock.

index.title: Programs
index.intro: Four STEAM programs for students aged 11–17. Each one ends with the students' own project, presented on location.
index.metaDescription: Orlando STEAM League, Europe STEAM League, STEAM League AI and Tokyo STEAM Championship: dates, destinations and content.

detail.priceOnRequest: Ask us about pricing and payment plans.
detail.ctaBody: We'll walk you through dates, places and how to enroll.

orlando-steam-league.summary: Students design a space colony while working across five theme parks, NASA's Kennedy Space Center and the UCF campus, where they spend two full academic days.

pathway.S: Coding at the Digital Hub and the physics behind Disney's Hollywood Studios
pathway.T: Six-degrees-of-freedom workshop at Universal and robotics with Ozobots
pathway.E: Environmental engineering at Epic Universe and a coaster design inspired by VelociCoaster (Islands of Adventure)
pathway.A: Art of Animation: colony layout and space-suit design

visits: Two academic days on the UCF campus
inclusions: Meals during the academic program (except three meals)
Software and materials (students bring their own laptop)
orlando-steam-league.rooms: Gender-split rooms of 2–4 students (up to 5 in suites). 10 pm curfew.

europe-steam-league.summary: Twelve days in the UK building a digital STEAM career portfolio, based on the Woldingham School campus with an excursion to Oxford.
visits: Red Bull Racing behind the scenes
inclusions: The Lion King and Arsenal Stadium tickets

steam-league-ai.summary: An artificial-intelligence innovation studio at Bradfield College, with projects aligned to the Sustainable Development Goals.

tokyo-steam-championship.tagline: Building Solutions for Better Cities and Communities
tokyo-steam-championship.summary: The top 20 winning schools from past leagues prepare for six months and present solutions for better cities and communities in Tokyo. Held every two years; the winning team gets a cash prize and Coded's support to implement its project.
